title: Latency Padding Harmonizer and Kernel Probe Playbook to Reduce Jitter in Continuous Batching
creator: Ethan Liu
description:
Problem:
Continuous batching in the runtime shows intermittent high tail-latency (p99 spikes) driven by two correlated phenomena: 1) small groups of requests creating 'odd-shaped' batch tensors that force kernel fallbacks or suboptimal kernel paths; 2) decode-time jitter introduced by KV-cache and attention recomputation when prefill streams are misaligned.

Proposal summary:
Introduce a two-part mitigation: (A) Latency Padding Harmonizer — a lightweight slot-level padding and micro-scheduling layer that normalizes token-length distributions into kernel-friendly shapes without materially increasing token work; (B) Kernel Probe Playbook — an empirical probing and heuristics library that picks kernel variants proactively (and warms them) based on short-run telemetry (sequence-length histogram, attention pattern signatures) to avoid late kernel switches during a decode.

Why different from past work:
Existing tickets address admission, shaping, and kernel affinity but tend to focus on coarse-grained batch shaping or admission throttles. This ticket focuses on "micro-harmonization": minimal padding plus micro-reordering within admission windows to maximize contiguous tensor shapes for the most efficient kernel, combined with a low-overhead probe-and-warm strategy so the runtime doesn't change kernels mid-decode. The approach aims for low risk (doesn't change model weights or quantization) and incremental rolloutability.
acceptance_criteria: p95 latency unchanged or improved, p99 reduced by >= 20% on our synthetic jitter workload
token-cost overhead <= 0.5% measured over 24h of production traffic (can be toggled per-tenant)
no regressions on throughput windows with long sequences (seq_len > 1024)
feature gated with canary rollout to 5% traffic and rollback flag
unit + integration tests for harmonizer logic and kernel probe playbook included
technical_decisions: Pad-to-profile: round up short sequences to the nearest kernel-preferred width but cap added padding to <16 tokens
Slot re-sequencing: allow reorder inside the admission window when it yields >12% contiguous tensor shape improvement; maintain original client ordering via metadata for decode assembly
Probe warm policy: measure kernel throughput for 50 preceding admissions of similar shape; if warm status unknown then launch a cheap probe trace (<10 warm tokens) ahead of live requests
Fallback safety: if probe fails or latency increases >15% for a 1-minute window, revert to previous kernel and mark the probed kernel as unstable
Visibility: expose harmonizer metrics (pad_added_tokens, reorders_applied, probe_success_rate) to console runtime-dashboard
experiment_results: Bench (synth-jitter-v2): baseline p99=420ms, harmonizer-only p99=340ms (-19%), harmonizer+probe p99=318ms (-24%)
Token overhead measured in bench: harmonizer-only +0.32%, harmonizer+probe +0.42%
Throughput at seq_len=2048: <1% regression in tokens/sec after enabling harmonizer (within noise)
Kernel-switch events observed: baseline 4.1 per 10k decodes, with probe reduced to 0.3 per 10k decodes
rollout_plan: 2) Internal perf lab run across GPU families (A100, H100, RTX8000) — 48h runs (done for A100/H100, need RTX)
3) Canary rollout: enable for 3% of production traffic for 24h, monitor p95/p99, probe success rate, pad_added_tokens
4) Expand to 25% for 72h if canary stable, then to 100% over 7 days with staggered regional waves
5) Post-rollout: 30-day observability collection and cost audit; follow-up optimizations based on kernel-profile feedback
